title: Du'a for Leaving the House
arabic: بسم الله توكلت على الله، لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله
transliteration: Bismillah, tawakkaltu ala Allah, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
translation: In the name of Allah, I trust in Allah; there is no might and no power except with Allah.
reference: Sunan Abu Dawud 5095, Sunan At-Tirmidhi, Sunan An-Nasa'i, Riyad as-Salihin 83
commentary: Sayyiduna Anas ibn Malik (radiyallahu ‘anhu) reports that Rasulullah ﷺ said, 'Whoever recites this dua, it is proclaimed to him: You have been guided, sufficed, and protected — and Shaytan leaves his path.'

title: Du'a for Entering the House
arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَلَجْنَا، وَبِسْمِ اللَّهِ خَرَجْنَا، وَعَلَى اللَّهِ رَبِّنَا تَوَكَّلْنَا
transliteration: Bismillahi walajna, wa bismillahi kharajna, wa 'ala Allahi Rabbina tawakkalna
translation: In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon our Lord we place our trust.

title: Du'a for Entering the Mosque
translation: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.

title: Du'a for Leaving the Mosque
translation: O Allah, I ask You from Your bounty.
commentary: Both du'as are from the same hadith narrated by Abu Usaid in Sahih Muslim 713a.

title: Du'a for Beneficial Rain
translation: O Allah! Let it be a strong fruitful rain.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1032 (Book of Invoking Allah for Rain)
commentary: Narrated Aisha (RA): Whenever Allah's Messenger ﷺ saw the rain, he used to say, 'O Allah! Let it be a strong fruitful rain.'

title: Du'a for Travel
arabic: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ
transliteration: Subhan alladhi sakhkhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrineen, wa inna ila Rabbina lamunqaliboon
translation: Glory be to Him Who has subjected this to us, and we could never have it (by our efforts), and to our Lord, surely, must we return.

title: Du'a for Reaching Destination
arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
transliteration: A'ūdhu bi kalimāt-illāhi't-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq
translation: I seek refuge in the Perfect Words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
commentary: This supplication provides protection against evils and harm while at that location until one leaves the place.
